clue.text: It's a pain securing support to back a type of soap

indicators.note: securing means holding something tight inside, so the pain word wraps round the support word

parts.note: colic is a sharp pain in the abdomen

indicators.note: to back means the support word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that propping up a bar of soap is a painful chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses the support word; 'securing' then holds that reversal just after the first letter of the pain word. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic is a strong disinfectant soap made with phenol, once common in schools and hospitals.

clue.text: Previously expressed regret, with some minimal acknowledgement

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone once said sorry, if only with a grudging little nod.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, so it is regret as expressed in former times.

clue.text: One appearing twitchy, perhaps, and going to hide

definitions.text: One appearing twitchy, perhaps, and going to hide

parts.words: One appearing twitchy, perhaps, and going to hide
parts.note: a twitcher is slang for an obsessive bird-spotter, and a hide is the screened shelter from which such enthusiasts watch

explanation.surface: A nervous person keeps vanishing into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen bird-spotters are nicknamed twitchers and sit in hides to observe wildlife unseen.

clue.text: Sparked off one lot attending to take action

parts.note: a fire sparked off has been lit
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is the number of people attending a sporting event

explanation.surface: A crowd, roused by a spark, decides to do something about it.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is the British term for the attendance (or takings) at a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take legal action, bringing a case before the courts.

clue.text: A certain point in a mass where it's particularly solemn

definitions.text: A certain point in a mass
definitions.meaning: the physics sense: the point through which a body's weight acts
read playfully as the heart of gravity, that is, the core of solemnity

explanation.definitionFit: In physics it is the balance point of an object; whimsically, it is the very middle of seriousness.

clue.text: Legal expert, in a state, simply having to get over it

indicators.note: in places the state's abbreviation inside the word for simply

parts.note: just means simply, as in just get over it
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone in a fluster is told they just have to get over it, legally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to get over it' completes the picture of 'just get over it' and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A jurist is a person learned in law, such as a judge or legal scholar.

clue.text: Bandied words, possibly, as pint's almost finished

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a pint of beer

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: gone means finished, used up

explanation.surface: Words get tossed around in the pub as the beer runs low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GONE to GON. A JAR is everyday British slang for a pint of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialist talk, words tossed around among insiders, hence bandied words, possibly.

clue.text: Port or whisky?

definitions.meaning: One of the Cinque Ports on England's south coast
... is a whisky distilled mainly from ... grain

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks a barman's question about drinks, but Port is a harbour town, not the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a historic East Sussex harbour town and also an American style of grain whisky.

clue.text: Promenade in street, and have to appear unsophisticated

indicators.note: in puts the promenade word inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a mall is a sheltered walk or promenade, as in The Mall in London
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Strolling along a street makes one look provincial.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-town attitudes are provincial and narrow, lacking big-city polish.

clue.text: Recite standard rubbish

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
rot means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses reciting as the usual nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, as a recitation without understanding.

clue.text: Invader overrunning south-east, or one attacking north-east?

indicators.note: overrunning means spreading over and around, so the invader encloses the compass letters

parts.note: the Normans invaded England in 1066

explanation.surface: Raiders swarm over the south-east, or perhaps attack the north-east instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Viking raiders struck north-east England, as at Lindisfarne.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were Viking raiders from Scandinavia who famously attacked the coasts of north-east England.

clue.text: A slant on retrieving a fortnight at least, essentially wasted

indicators.note: essentially points to the very centre of the word, which is thrown away
retrieving suggests bringing back, so the word for the period is read in reverse

parts.note: a fortnight is two weeks, so at least that span is weeks in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone gives a biased take on recovering a mostly wasted two weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrieving' turns WEEKS into SKEEW; 'essentially wasted' removes its middle letter, an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A skew is a slant or bias, as in a skewed view of events.

clue.text: Ugly woman meeting French writer in Italian town

parts.note: a gorgon is a fierce or ugly woman, after Medusa and her sisters
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A plain woman bumps into a French author in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a town near Milan in Lombardy, which gave its name to the blue cheese.

clue.text: Old type of suit on, entertaining — board, serving seafood

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, holding a guest inside, so the board goes within

parts.note: the zoot suit was a baggy 1940s fashion
a plank is a board

explanation.surface: A man in an old-fashioned suit serves seafood from a wooden platter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts the board inside the suit-plus-on pair, after its first three letters. Zooplankton as seafood is a playful sense: food found in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Zooplankton are tiny drifting sea animals, the food of whales and fish, hence seafood in a playful sense.

clue.text: That trebled the answer a fantastic computer gave

definitions.text: That trebled the answer a fantastic computer gave

parts.words: That trebled the answer a fantastic computer gave
parts.note: that is the clue's own number, fourteen, which tripled gives the reply the computer Deep Thought gives in The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

explanation.surface: A science-fiction machine offers a famously odd reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That' refers to the clue number 14; three times 14 is the number Douglas Adams' computer Deep Thought gives as the Answer to Life, the Universe and Everything.
explanation.definitionFit: In Douglas Adams' comic fantasy, the supercomputer Deep Thought computes this number as the ultimate answer.

clue.text: Seriously disliked dealing with stink raised over relocation of Sioux

indicators.note: relocation means moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means about or dealing with, as in a book on birds

indicators.note: raised over in a down clue means the letters are turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink

explanation.surface: A stink kicked up over the resettling of the Sioux was much resented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised over' turns BO into OB, which leads; 'relocation of' then rearranges the pool, ON with SIOUX giving NOXIOUS after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or offensive, and so heartily disliked.

clue.text: Someone playing Blowin' in the Wind

definitions.text: Someone playing Blowin' in the Wind

parts.words: Someone playing Blowin' in the Wind
parts.note: the song title is read literally: a player blowing in the woodwind section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: A musician performs Bob Dylan's protest song.
explanation.walkthrough: Oboe can mean an oboist, the player, and the oboe is a woodwind instrument that is blown.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can denote the oboist as well as the instrument, a reed player in the woodwind section.

clue.text: States led by intractable individual in hellish situation

indicators.note: led by means the second piece comes after the first in a down clue

parts.note: a tartar is a fierce, difficult person
US is the United States

explanation.surface: America follows a stubborn leader into a hellish predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartarus is the abyss of the Greek underworld where the wicked are punished, a hell.

clue.text: Not very far from an island

definitions.meaning: a small distance, as in moving only a little way
in Scotland and Ireland an ... is a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.walkthrough: INCH as a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth, is less familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny distance; in Scottish place names it also means a small island.

clue.text: Niggardly, denying daughter cooked fish

indicators.note: cooked means doctored or altered, so the letters are rearranged
denying means refusing entry, so the letter is removed

explanation.surface: A stingy cook refuses his daughter any fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing D from NIGGARDLY leaves NIGGARLY, and 'cooked' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater fish of the salmon family with a large dorsal fin.

clue.text: Go after victory, somehow keeping cool

indicators.note: after places the attempt word behind the victory word

parts.note: a win is a victory
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: After winning, someone keeps calm and has another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow keeping' is linking padding here; WIN followed by TRY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wintry weather is cold, so the word fits cool in the sense of chilly.

clue.text: Go out with soldier, taking in ball that's overpriced

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing something within, so the ball goes inside

parts.note: to exit is to go out
an orb is a ball or sphere
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: Leaving with a soldier, someone picks up a ball that cost far too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts the ball inside the go-out word; the soldier is a soldier ant, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant prices are excessively high, far beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Call a celebrity

definitions.meaning: to call is to give a title or label to

explanation.definitionFit: To name is to call by a title, and a famous person is a name, as in household name.

clue.text: Turned over more than half of fruit to find larger one

indicators.text: Turned over more than half of
indicators.note: turned over means read backwards, and more than half of limits the turn to the first three of five letters

parts.note: a lemon is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone flips most of a fruit and discovers a bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing LEM, the first three letters of LEMON, gives MEL, leaving ON in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a much larger fruit than a lemon, so it is the larger one.

clue.text: Little coverage of new union in the paper

definitions.text: Little coverage of new union in the paper

parts.words: Little coverage of new union in the paper
parts.note: reads like poor press reporting of a wedding, but describes the tiny pieces of paper scattered over newlyweds

explanation.surface: A newspaper barely reports on a recently formed trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is a marriage; 'in the paper' means made of paper, not printed in a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is little pieces of coloured paper thrown over a newly married couple.

clue.text: Remote agricultural business terminally neglected

indicators.note: terminally means at the end, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: a farm is an agricultural business

explanation.surface: A distant farm has been let go at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Far means distant or remote, a long way off.

clue.text: Make nervous sound

definitions.meaning: a rapid series of short clattering noises

explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve them, and a rattle is a clattering noise.

clue.text: Flier in old jet that's noisy

indicators.note: noisy points to how the letters are pronounced when spoken

parts.note: O is old, and a spray is a jet of liquid

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that an old jet aircraft is loud.
explanation.walkthrough: O (old) plus SPRAY (jet) said out loud matches one common pronunciation of the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: So are feet metric?

parts.note: feet as units of length are imperial, not metric, but feet in verse make up a metre, so the answer to the question is both

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether feet belong to the metric system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' stands for an equivocal reply; the poetic sense of feet as units of metre makes the question two-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an equivocal reply, both affirmative and negative, fitting a question true in one sense and false in another.
